## Why skills only, not the whole project

Superpowers also ships `CLAUDE.md`, `hooks/`, `.claude-plugin/`,
`.opencode/plugins/`, per-agent extension directories, and a release-notes file.
None of it is vendored:

- Its `CLAUDE.md` is contributor guidance for **its own** repository, including
  a PR-rejection policy addressed to agents opening issues upstream. Adopting it
  here would impose rules that have nothing to do with this repository.
- `hooks/` and the plugin manifests assume a specific installation layout and a
  specific agent runtime. They would be the first thing to break on a new
  agent, and a broken hook is worse than no hook.
- Vendoring only `skills/` keeps the useful part small, reviewable, and
  diffable against upstream.

## Local divergences

None inside the skill files: they are byte-identical to upstream. The
divergences are all in `AGENTS.md`, which is where an agent looks first.

| Upstream behaviour | Local rule | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Plans go to `docs/superpowers/plans/` | Go to `tasks/` or `docs/` | This repository has its own task system and document graph; a second plan location would rot |
| `brainstorming` and `writing-plans` pause for design approval | Superseded for research, experiment, and infrastructure work | Decision `D003`: ordinary design review does not need a human; authorization does |
| `using-superpowers` bootstraps from plugin metadata | Skills are discovered from the repository | No plugin install step exists here |

## Line-cap exemptions

Vendored files are exempt from the 300-line documentation cap so that they can
stay byte-identical to upstream and remain diffable. Lint reports them as
`info` with their line counts, so the exception stays visible.

Five vendored files exceed 300 lines:

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `.agents/skills/writing-skills/anthropic-best-practices.md` | 1150 |
| `.agents/skills/writing-skills/SKILL.md` | 679 |
| `.agents/skills/subagent-driven-development/SKILL.md` | 503 |
| `.agents/skills/writing-skills/testing-skills-with-subagents.md` | 384 |
| `.agents/skills/test-driven-development/SKILL.md` | 320 |

# Raw instrument captures. Same class as `.json` and `.log`: bytes an external
# endpoint returned, written before parsing, never hand-edited, and the reason a
# figure in a results.json can be traced to the request that produced it. E020's
# 82 captures are the reason; the rule is the extension, not the experiment.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/raw/*.sse
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/raw/*.sse.stderr

# Raw *documentation* captures, added by E028. The same class again: bytes an
# external endpoint returned, written before parsing, never hand-edited, and the
# reason a reader's `does_not_serve` verdict can be traced to the text it was
# read from. `.txt` because a README and a web page are both plain text after
# tag-stripping, and stripping is part of the capture, so the stored bytes are
# what the reader was shown.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/raw/docs/*.txt

## Updating a vendored set

1. Read the upstream release notes for the target version.
2. Re-copy `skills/` from a clean clone of the tag.
3. Update the version, commit, and commit date above.
4. Run `tools/origin skills hash` then `tools/origin skills verify`.
5. Run `tools/origin skills sync` if any skill was added or removed, so the
   `.claude/skills` mirrors match.
6. Re-read every local divergence in `AGENTS.md` and confirm it still makes
   sense against the new version.

Drift against **upstream** cannot be detected offline; `skills verify` only
detects local modification of what is recorded in `hashes.json`. Checking
upstream is step 1 of an update, deliberately a human decision.
